questions.stem: Strategy A strictly dominates strategy B when…
options: A gives a higher payoff than B whatever the other players do
A gives a higher payoff than B for at least one choice of the others
A is the strategy most players choose
A and B give the same payoff on average
questions.explanation: Strict dominance means better in every case, against every combination of the other players' strategies (Slide 3).
questions.hint: 'Whatever the others do' is the key phrase.

questions.stem: Why is the Prisoner's Dilemma a dilemma?
options: Each player's dominant strategy leads to an outcome both would want to avoid
Neither player has a dominant strategy
The payoffs are unknown to the players
Cooperating is dominant but players defect anyway
questions.explanation: Defect dominates for each player, but mutual defection is worse for both than mutual cooperation (Slide 4).
questions.hint: Compare what each does individually with what is best jointly.

questions.stem: What does iterated elimination of strictly dominated strategies assume?
options: Players are rational and know the others are rational too
Every game has a dominant strategy for every player
questions.explanation: Each round of elimination relies on players knowing the others won't play dominated strategies, which needs rationality to be common knowledge (Slide 5).
questions.hint: Why would a strategy become dominated only after another player's strategy is removed?
